title: VDCores Qwen3 1.7B RepeatM State Lite Diagnostic
command: Apply a tmp-only VDCores diagnostic patch on the H200 baseline checkout, rebuild with DAE_DIAG_REPEAT_STATE_LITE and DAE_DIAG_WAIT_AFTER_WB_ALLOC, then run CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 QWEN1P7B_NO_PREFETCH=all QWEN1P7B_LOGITS_SPLIT_M=6 python app/python/qwen3_1p7b/sched.py --hf-cache-dir <shared-hf-cache> --debug-num-layers 1 --debug-stop-after logits -N 1 --launch.
observation: The lite RepeatM diagnostic rebuilt on H200 and reproduced the direct logits failure without changing addr_accum semantics. PC49 decoded as reg_start=0, reg_end=5, size=2, address=0x1000000000, and set lane-0 gpr1 to 0. PC50 then consumed source lane 0 but addr_accum was 0x7fffff, producing desc33 coordinates (65535,127,0) and ending with illegal instruction.
blocker: VDCores still cannot import queue/resource-policy timing. The latest evidence rules out bad PC49 RepeatM field encoding and localizes the bad coordinate to allocwarp RepeatM accumulator transport between decode and consumers. The split-shuffle diagnostic was not a complete fix, so the next step is a non-perturbing native 64-bit shuffle/register transport isolation or a targeted 32-bit packed-coordinate transport experiment.

rules_out: incorrect pc49 RepeatM field encoding for reg range, count, and delta
writeback slot metadata lifetime as the only remaining logits blocker
the split 64-bit shuffle variant as a complete fix
summary.next_debug_target: inspect the native 64-bit shuffle/register transport in allocwarp with a non-perturbing reproduction, then test a lane-0-only split transport or explicit 32-bit packed-coordinate transport for RepeatM consumers before importing VDCores timing
